title: odometer
gist: A speedrun for training a small language model, with a meter where the clock would be. Every tensor operation costs ticks priced from its shape, so a laptop and a server stop at the same reading, and a record has to survive a rerun on fresh seeds.
summary: Lets a person or a coding agent try to beat a training record on hardware they own, and lets anyone check a record from a clean clone.

hero_image.alt: The record table as a ladder: test bits per byte falling from 1.7058 for the small GPT recipe to 1.0887 for the current record, with the 6 newest rows marked as written by agents.

site.eyebrow: Training speedrun · 40 billion ticks · 6 agent attempts · MIT
site.blurb: A speedrun where every tensor operation costs ticks priced from its shape, so hardware only buys finishing sooner. Coding agents took the record from 1.1555, the best recipe, to 1.0887 bits per byte, and 5 of 7 claims in the registered series cleared the record rule. The recipes were ported with an agent too and no person has run the track, so nothing here compares agents with people.
